name: Margaret River
objection: Most of its draws (wineries, caves, beaches) lie outside the inland town and will be their own spots; the town risks being a wrapper. Proposer decides destination vs spot; also the 'Margaret River wine region' candidate is the same name (kept as one here).

name: Yallingup
objection: Its draws (Ngilgi Cave, Yallingup Beach, Injidup Natural Spa, Canal Rocks) are separate candidates; listing the town beside them may be a wrapper (COVERAGE 'a town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw').

name: Augusta
objection: No Wikivoyage article of its own (404); its headline draw, Cape Leeuwin Lighthouse, is a separate spot.

name: Pemberton
objection: Its draws (Gloucester Tree, Beedelup Falls, Bicentennial Tree) are separate spots.

name: Donnybrook
objection: A farming town most travellers pass through on the highway; its one named draw (the Apple Fun Park) is a playground.

name: Harvey
objection: Agricultural town with no single headline sight; visitors mostly stop briefly on the South Western Highway. Arguably review.

name: Bridgetown
objection: Best known for the Blues at Bridgetown festival, which is an event and does not count; town draws are modest (main street, galleries).

name: Manjimup
objection: Only one counted source family found; its best sights (Diamond Tree, King Jarrah, Heritage Park) are separate places.

name: Nannup
objection: Small village; one substantive counted source; draws are low-key (heritage walk, galleries).

name: Balingup
objection: Tiny village; Golden Valley Tree Park is its main sight and may be its own spot.

name: Boyup Brook
objection: Against: one counted source and nothing specific to see or do (brief: a town with nothing a source names is reject or review). For: a listed town of the regional board, gateway for country-music events (events do not count).

name: Northcliffe
objection: For: gateway to D'Entrecasteaux NP and Windy Harbour with a named art trail and museum. Against: one counted source, and its named draws (Understory, Mount Chudalup) are separate candidates, so the town may be a wrapper.

name: Australind
objection: Against: one local-government tourism source; a residential satellite of Bunbury ('Australia's fastest growing regional location') with cafes and a big pub; a traveller from elsewhere rarely goes out of their way for it. For: estuary jetty and eco museum.

name: Gracetown
objection: Small hamlet; its beach ('Gracetown Beach') is the same place, so keep one (town or beach), not both.

name: Prevelly
objection: Against: its headline draw is Surfers Point (kept separately), so the village is likely a wrapper or near-duplicate (COVERAGE: never list a town beside its own attraction). For: a named surf village with its own beaches and river mouth.

name: Hamelin Bay
objection: Wild stingrays are the main draw and not guaranteed; the village itself is a caravan park and boat ramp.

name: Cowaramup
objection: Mostly shops and cafés in a pass-through town on Bussell Highway; the cows are a short photo stop.

name: Wonnerup House
objection: Open only two days a week, and the furnishings are in storage during reinterpretation, so the visit is thinner than it was.

name: Old Butter Factory and Busselton Museum
objection: A local-history museum; a traveller would go only if already in Busselton.

name: St Mary's Church Busselton
objection: For: a landmark guides single out, with a graveyard to explore. Against: the board files it under 'local services', it is a working parish church mostly seen from outside, and the visit is about 15 minutes.

name: Meelup Regional Park
objection: Meelup Beach is the draw and may be its own candidate; if both are kept they overlap (keep one, the beach or the park), and Eagle Bay, Castle Rock and Bunker Bay sit inside the park.

name: Eagle Bay
objection: Partly inside Meelup Regional Park; one of several similar calm Geographe Bay beaches.

name: Bunker Bay
objection: No coordinates in the candidate; overlaps the Cape Naturaliste walks (Bunker Bay loop) and is mostly known for its resort.

name: Koombana Beach
objection: For: wild dolphins at the beach. Against: Wikivoyage calls it 'a modest beach', and the dolphin interaction zone and visitor facilities are the Dolphin Discovery Centre on the same beach, so it is a near-duplicate of that spot.

name: Dolphin Discovery Centre
objection: Wild dolphins are not guaranteed and the cruises are an operator product; the place is the centre and beach, which is what is kept.

name: Cape Leeuwin
objection: Not a separate place from Cape Leeuwin Lighthouse: visitors reach the cape at the lighthouse precinct (ticketed grounds, interpretive centre), which is listed separately by Wikivoyage and the board. Keep as ONE spot (the lighthouse, with 'where two oceans meet' in its bio) rather than both; review only to decide which name carries it.

name: Cape Naturaliste
objection: Shares its car park and precinct with Cape Naturaliste Lighthouse, listed separately; the walks are short sections of the Cape to Cape Track. Keep as one with the lighthouse unless the owner wants the headland walks as their own spot.

name: Canal Rocks
objection: A short stop (30 minutes) on the coast road near Yallingup.

name: Injidup Natural Spa
objection: Only a 'spa' at the right tide and swell, and dangerous in big seas; no coordinates in the candidate.

name: Yallingup Beach
objection: Overlaps the Yallingup town candidate (the beach is the town's draw); keep the beach or the town as the spot, not a wrapper. No coordinates in the candidate.

name: Smiths Beach
objection: One counted source; its coordinates are Yallingup's town point (Wikipedia redirects to Yallingup), so the pin must be resolved afresh.

name: Surfers Point
objection: The WSL contest is an event and does not count; the place itself is a surf break and lookout, a 30-minute stop.

name: Redgate Beach
objection: One counted source; unpatrolled surf beach with dangerous rips.

name: Ferguson Valley
objection: An area rather than one place; Gnomesville and Wellington National Park are separate candidates, so the proposer must decide whether it is a destination or a spot.

name: Leeuwin Estate
objection: Still a winery among 200+; its famous concerts are events and do not count.

name: Cape Mentelle Vineyards
objection: For: a founding estate a board names. Against: a cellar door like dozens of others, with no visitor attraction beyond tasting; the brief keeps a winery only when singled out as a destination in its own right.

name: Vasse Felix
objection: A winery and restaurant; the gallery is the non-tasting draw.

name: Voyager Estate
objection: For: a well-known estate with tours. Against: tastings and dining only; no source read singles it out as a destination beyond the cellar door (brief winery rule).

name: Cullen Wines
objection: For: two counted sources, a pioneer estate. Against: a cellar door and restaurant like many others; the brief keeps a winery only when singled out as a destination.

name: Calgardup Cave
objection: Less famous than Jewel, Lake, Mammoth and Ngilgi; a short self-guided visit.

name: Giants Cave
objection: Open only some months (closed May-Sep except school holidays): a seasonal venue, which still counts.

name: Jewel Cave
objection: None significant; one of four commercial show caves.

name: Wadandi Track
objection: Only one counted source and that is a council page, not a tourism or guide listing; the trail is incomplete until 2028 and the note placed it 'around Augusta', whereas the open sections are Busselton and Cowaramup; may be better added once finished. Case for: state-funded flagship trail the region is promoting.

name: Boranup Forest
objection: It is part of Leeuwin-Naturaliste National Park; if the park itself is a spot the forest could read as a sub-part. But the guides treat it as its own named stop.

name: Gloucester Tree
objection: DBCA notes a South West Climbing Trees Project to upgrade platforms and reopen the trees to climbing, so climbing may be intermittently closed; the tree, walks and picnic area remain open whatever.

name: Beedelup Falls
objection: Falls are seasonal (best in winter and spring) and the boardwalk area is a short visit; but two counted sources and the loop walk make it a full stop.

name: King Jarrah Heritage Trail
objection: Short visit (about 30 min) at a single tree on the edge of town; arguably a local picnic reserve.

name: Shannon National Park
objection: Only one counted source (the agency's own page) and 706 views; a quieter park than Warren or Gloucester.

name: Warren National Park
objection: The Dave Evans Bicentennial Tree is its headline; if the tree is listed separately, the park could be a near-duplicate. The Bicentennial Tree is not in this shard, so the park carries it here.

name: Gloucester National Park
objection: Near-duplicate of the Gloucester Tree, which is what visitors come for and which sits in it; one counted source (the agency's own page). Keep only if the Cascades/trails are not carried by the tree spot.

name: Blackwood River National Park
objection: One counted source; the park is a string of river campgrounds rather than a single draw, and paddling the Blackwood is equally done from Nannup or Augusta; may be better as 'Blackwood River' with its access point.

name: Wellington National Park
objection: Holds Wellington Dam and Honeymoon Pool, which are judged separately; risk of three overlapping spots. A clear park in its own right.

name: Wellington Dam
objection: Lies inside Wellington National Park, also kept; could be folded into the park's bio. The mural makes it a named sight in its own right.

name: Honeymoon Pool
objection: Inside Wellington National Park, about 10 km from Wellington Dam; a third Wellington spot could be thin. Swimming and camping make it a distinct stop.

name: Mount Frankland National Park
objection: One counted source and modest views (679/yr); the draw is really the Wilderness Lookout and summit walk, so if the run also has 'Mount Frankland Wilderness Lookout' or 'Mount Frankland summit' as a candidate, keep only one (the park, pinned at the lookout car park) as a duplicate. Small park: per COVERAGE it is a standalone spot, not a destination.

name: D'Entrecasteaux National Park
objection: Huge linear park, much of it 4WD-only; it needs a single visitor point (Point D'Entrecasteaux/Windy Harbour) and the eastern end (Mandalay Beach) is Great Southern.

name: Yeagarup Dunes
objection: Inside D'Entrecasteaux National Park (also kept), and the dunes proper need a 4WD; a 2WD visitor sees only the lake boardwalk at the dunes' edge.

name: Lake Muir National Park
objection: A highway rest stop with a 15-30 minute boardwalk; the lake can be a dry bed in summer. Only the agency page plus a local tourism listing.

name: Black Diamond Pool
objection: Shire signs warn of low pH and bacteria (naegleria traces) and it has had a drowning; swimming is at your own risk. Not closed per any source found.

name: Harris Dam
objection: One counted source; Wikivoyage itself says 'look is all you can do' (no water activities): a picnic area by a water-supply dam, mostly local use.

name: Glen Mervyn Dam
objection: One counted source; a local boating and camping reservoir that visitors from elsewhere rarely travel for.

name: Minninup Pool
objection: One counted source; a local swimming hole, and Collie already has stronger swimming spots (Black Diamond, Stockton Lake, Honeymoon Pool).

name: Stockton Lake
objection: A near-twin of Black Diamond Pool 10 km away (both former mine lakes for swimming); the owner may want only one.

name: Collie River Walk
objection: One line in one source; a town riverside path, more a local amenity than a draw from elsewhere.

name: Collie Railway Museum
objection: One counted source and a small volunteer museum; a 30-minute stop only if passing through Collie.

name: Coalfields Museum
objection: One counted source; a small local-history museum; Collie's coal heritage is its one distinct theme.

name: Capes Raptor Centre
objection: Successor to Eagles Heritage at the same Boodjidup Rd site: make sure it is not a duplicate of an existing Eagles Heritage spot (same place, new name - keep one entry). Closed Tuesdays outside school holidays.

name: Wambenger Trails
objection: Lies inside Wellington National Park: if the park is kept as a destination this is its spot, and as a whole network it overlaps the park itself (risk of near-duplicate); pin needs a trailhead/midpoint choice.

name: Ellensbrook Homestead
objection: Short visit and limited opening days (closed in 38-degree heat); the candidate note says 'near Augusta' but it is off Caves Road north of Margaret River (Ellen Brook Rd) - fix the pin.

name: Boola Bidi Dreaming Centre
objection: Opened recently and partly a visitor-servicing centre; guided walks may need booking. Open five days a week.

name: Aerial Adventure Pemberton
objection: Against: it is an operator's activity course inside Gloucester National Park, next to the Gloucester Tree (risk of being part of that larger spot); paid, booked activity; closes for a winter break. For: a fixed permanent venue, like an amusement park, that visitors travel to Pemberton for.

name: Blackwood River
objection: A long linear feature: it needs a main visitor access point (Nannup town reach or Wrights Bridge), not the Wikipedia centroid near Augusta; overlaps any Nannup/Bridgetown town spot and Barrabup Pool if listed separately.

name: Nannup Lavender Farm and Campground
objection: Against: mostly a café, gift shop and campground with only seasonal flowering and garden; one-hour stop only if nearby anyway. For: a recognisable farm-gate attraction two regional tourism sources list.

name: Bunbury Wildlife Park
objection: Only one counted source opened (board; the operator page is the city's own); a modest council park that may be only 'if nearby' for out-of-towners.

name: Meelup Beach
objection: Possibly a near-duplicate of a Meelup Regional Park or Meelup Beach spot already listed; check before adding.

name: Origins Market
objection: Trading days unconfirmed (may be only a few days a week, which fails rule 4); it is essentially a food hall and shops (rule 2). Keep only if it trades daily like a market hall.

name: Bunbury Regional Art Gallery
objection: A regional gallery with rotating exhibitions; a 'only if you are nearby' stop for many visitors.

name: A Maze'n Margaret River
objection: Only one counted source names it; a family amusement stop that two other mazes in the area duplicate in kind (Yallingup Maze). Marginal: friend test passes only for families.

name: Golden Valley Tree Park
objection: Volunteer-run community arboretum; best in autumn colour, quieter otherwise.

name: Bunbury Museum and Heritage Centre
objection: Only one counted visitor source; a modest town museum.

name: Understory Art & Nature Trail
objection: Small paid community trail in a remote village.

name: Manjimup Heritage Park & Power Up Museum
objection: Partly a town park with playground; museums are small.

name: Yallingup Maze
objection: Family amusement; adults without kids would not go out of their way. Could be review rather than keep.

name: Lake Cave
objection: None of substance; one of several show caves in the area but a distinct cave.

name: Sugarloaf Rock
objection: Short stop (15-30 min), on the Cape to Cape Track; but agency singles it out by name.

name: Gnomesville
objection: Short stop; partly damaged by a November 2024 flood and under restoration.

name: Wyalup-Rocky Point
objection: A short stop beside the town beach (Back Beach); 15-30 minutes.

name: Gnarabup Beach
objection: Second-tier beach; a near neighbour of Prevelly/Surfers Point if those are listed.

name: Big Brook Dam
objection: A local recreation reservoir; mostly a picnic/walk stop.

name: Torpedo Rocks
objection: Part of a larger walk (Torpedo Trail / Cape to Cape) and a short lookout; one source; could be folded into Yallingup or the Cape to Cape spot ('What qualifies' 3).

name: Cape Leeuwin Waterwheel
objection: A 10-15 minute stop beside the lighthouse; could be treated as part of Cape Leeuwin.

name: Fernhook Falls
objection: Only one counted source and no Wikipedia article; in summer the falls are a trickle, so the draw is seasonal and it sits on a remote forest road. Also has a campground on site: keep the falls as the place, not the campground.

name: Mandalay Beach
objection: One counted source and no Wikipedia article; the wreck is only visible at low tide, and it is a gravel-road detour off the South Western Highway.

name: Peppermint Grove Beach
objection: One counted source; it is a small holiday settlement's local beach on a 29 km stretch of similar Geographe Bay coast, and most of the board's copy promotes the holiday park beside it. A friend flying in would go only if staying nearby: arguable, but the rule keeps beaches a board names.
